statement: Kernel-checked adaptive final theorem: if 0<theta<1 satisfies the source short-prime input PI(theta), then every fixed 0<c<(1-theta)/3 gives, for all sufficiently large k and every 2k<n<=exp(c(log k)^2/loglog k), a prime divisor p in (k,k+3k^theta) of (n-k)...(n-1), hence p in (k,2k). The proof constructs the actual positive-real max scale, least stopping order, uniform r>=2 third/additive asymptotics, and complete four-range package. The older balanced class still has exact window 9/23<theta<1, so 9/23 is now confirmed as a balanced-scale artifact. The explicitly defined location-blind adaptive subdivided Konyagin little-o certificate class still cannot reach c>=(1-theta)/3. At theta=21/40 the unconditional BHP corollary remains every c<19/120; Erdős 451 itself is not closed.

dependency_gaps: The abstract theta theorem assumes PI(theta); the theta=21/40 corollary imports the Baker--Harman--Pintz short-prime input exactly as the source paper does.

The complete adaptive four-range ParametricRangeBuilder and final PI(theta)-conditional theorem are kernel-checked in Lean for every 0<theta<1. The enlarged no-go remains natural-proof plus same-model cross-reconstruction rather than Lean or external review.

The enlarged no-go is confined to a location-blind deterministic-tail partition whose nonnegative Theorem 4.1 bounds are summed and required to be o(k^theta/log k). It does not cover sparse covers selected from actual prime locations, cross-block cancellation, stronger prime inputs, stronger exponential-sum estimates, or the true bad-set cardinality.
Novelty and publication priority remain unchecked.
